subject: Dedicated capacity options: min GPU footprint + activation schedules for NovaCare
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacare.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity options: min GPU footprint + activation schedules for NovaCare

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is an initial set of capacity options tuned to the workload numbers you shared (mixed chat + fine-tuned embed + reranking traffic). I structured three paths so you can pick the operational tradeoff that best fits your launch timeline and cost targets. High level:

- Option A (baseline): Small guaranteed pool to match day-1 peak for conversational surface. Fastest onboarding.
- Option B (phased growth): Moderate initial commit with automatic scale steps at month 3 and month 6. Good for predictable but growing production traffic.
- Option C (buffered runway): Larger minimum commit with surge/burst lanes and reserved buffer for seasonal spikes.

Key decision levers in the attached PDF: committed min GPUs, cluster layout (number and type), expected activation windows, and recommended quantization & batching settings to reduce token cost. I also included an SLO table (latency targets / burst capability) and a simple burn-rate estimate for each option.

Quick asks for us to finalize pricing and legal language:
1) Confirm which option you want to lean on.
2) Any constraint on absolute GPU types (we proposed A100 80GB for the primary lanes, with optional 4080 burst lanes).
3) Preferred start window (we can begin onboarding as early as 2 weeks after contract signature).

Attachments: novacare_capacity_options_v1.pdf (pdf), slo_and_burn_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

If you'd like, we can also prepare a one-page mutual action plan mapping milestones (kickoff, staging validation, go-live).

— Markus
Markus Klein

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacare.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novacare.ai
Date: 2026-10-13T11:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options: min GPU footprint + activation schedules for NovaCare

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the detailed doc. A few clarifying questions before we present to our CTO and procurement:

1) For Option B you show a month-3 scale to 16 GPUs and month-6 to 32 GPUs. Can you call out the expected raw throughput (tokens/sec or queries/sec) driving those steps and the latency SLOs at those levels? We need capacity numbers to justify the ramp.
2) Is the minimum-commit (billing baseline) enforced per cluster or can we split across two geographic pools for DR? Our legal team prefers cross-region minimums for resilience.
3) If we start with Option A, what is the shortest path to burst to Option C if adoption accelerates faster than projected? How fast can you provision additional lanes and what are the expected cost delta?

Also note procurement will request a clear on/off-ramps clause and an audit trail for capacity usage for the first 90 days.

Elena Ruiz
VP Product, NovaCare
elena@novacare.ai

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@novacare.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-14T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options: min GPU footprint + activation schedules for NovaCare

Elena —

Great questions. Short answers up front, details below.

1) Throughput and SLOs for Option B:
   - Month 0 (Option B baseline = 8 x A100-80GB): ~120 qps for short-chat requests (avg 64 tokens), 95th pct latency ~180ms per token at steady-state. Embedding and rerank jobs run on a dedicated queue; estimated throughput 220 embed/s with batching.
   - Month 3 (16 x A100): ~260 qps chat, 95th pct latency ~160ms per token due to additional headroom and longer batching windows.
   - Month 6 (32 x A100): ~540 qps chat, 95th pct latency ~150ms per token; embedding/rerank throughput scales roughly linearly with GPU count with minor efficiency gains from larger batch aggregation.

   These are conservative estimates based on model mix you provided (chat with model M-Redwood-1.3 + 7B embed variants). We include token-level telemetry so you can validate assumptions in staging.

2) Minimum-commit enforcement and cross-region split:
   - We can structure the contract two ways: a single regional cluster minimum, or a split-minimum across two zones (e.g., 60% primary / 40% DR). Split minimums are supported; the billing baseline applies to the sum of reserved GPUs across the two pools. DR pools run cold until activated (minutes to warm; we offer warm snapshots to reduce cold-start to under 3 minutes for KV-cache priming).

3) Fast burst path from Option A to Option C:
   - If you sign Option A and need to ramp quickly, we can provision additional burst lanes within 72 hours for incremental capacity (subject to regional availability). For a sustained upgrade (moving commit tiers), typical timeline is 7–14 days for contract amendment + provisioning and staging. Cost delta: burst lanes are billed at a slightly higher rate (on-demand tier) while sustained commit conversion applies discounted committed GPU pricing; we show both scenarios in the attached spreadsheet.

Audit trail and 90-day usage window: we can enable daily usage exports (CSV), token-level cost breakdown, and audit logs forwarded to your S3/GCS for procurement review.

Notes on optimization to reduce committed footprint: quantize non-critical models to 4-bit for retrained embeddings (saves 30–45% GPU memory), apply KV-prefix caching for chat sessions expected to have long context reuse, and set conservative batching windows during off-peak to push more throughput through fewer GPUs. We can help run a short eval (2-week pilot) to validate those levers before final commit.

I attached the updated SLO matrix and the burn-rate scenarios for each option. Happy to walk the CTO through the numbers live — we can do a 30-min deep-dive and show the telemetry dashboard.

— Markus

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options: min GPU footprint + activation schedules for NovaCare

Markus / Team —

I reviewed the numbers and spoke with pricing. A few commercial notes we should propose to NovaCare in the next deck:

- Recommend we position Option B as the default with a 9-month staircase: commit to 8g -> 16g @ month 3 -> 32g @ month 6 with a 30-day notice window for the month-6 step to give procurement flexibility. This provides a concrete path while keeping conversion simple.
- Offer a one-time onboarding credit equivalent to 2 GPU-weeks to help cover initial validation runs in staging (helps procurement sign-off).
- For split-region minimums, include an SLA credit if we miss warm-recovery targets (>5 min) for DR activations in the first 90 days.

I'll draft the updated pricing bullets and add to the deck. Markus — if you can confirm the qps/latency rows you gave are the ones we want in the MSA, we'll insert those as binding performance targets for the committed lanes.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
